subproblems.title: Localised three-term estimate for the rescaled area integrals
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P continuous, L : ℝ^n → ℝ^P continuous linear, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel, J : ℝ^n → ℝ Borel with 0 ≤ J ≤ K, m > 0, b ∈ ℝ^n, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, and R, M, r ∈ ℝ. Assume (labels (i) and (iii) as in the parent) (i) m|a − b| ≤ |F(a) − F(b)| for all a ∈ B; (iii) m|c| ≤ |Lc| for all c ∈ ℝ^n; f(w) = 0 whenever |w| ≥ R; |f(w)| ≤ M for all w; and r > 0. Write Φ_r(c) := r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b)) and D := B̄_{R/m}(0). Then |∫_{ℝ^n} 1_B(b + rc)·J(b + rc)·f(Φ_r(c)) dλ(c) − J(b)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Lc) dλ(c)| ≤ KM·∫_D 1_{ℝ^n∖B}(b + rc) dλ(c) + M·∫_D |J(b + rc) − J(b)| dλ(c) + J(b)·∫_D |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Lc)| dλ(c). Here λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n and all integrals are Bochner integrals.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (L : Euclid n →L[ℝ] Euclid P) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (J : Euclid n → ℝ) (K m : ℝ) (b : Euclid n) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (R M r : ℝ), Continuous F → MeasurableSet B → Measurable J → (∀ a, 0 ≤ J a ∧ J a ≤ K) → 0 < m → (∀ a ∈ B, m * ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖F a - F b‖) → (∀ c, m * ‖c‖ ≤ ‖L c‖) → Continuous f → (∀ w, R ≤ ‖w‖ → f w = 0) → (∀ w, ‖f w‖ ≤ M) → 0 < r → ‖(∫ c, B.indicator J (b + r • c) * f (r⁻¹ • (F (b + r • c) - F b)) ∂volume) - J b * (∫ c, f (L c) ∂volume)‖ ≤ K * M * (∫ c in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m), Bᶜ.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) (b + r • c) ∂volume) + M * (∫ c in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m), ‖J (b + r • c) - J b‖ ∂volume) + J b * (∫ c in closedBall (0 : Euclid n) (R / m), ‖f (r⁻¹ • (F (b + r • c) - F b)) - f (L c)‖ ∂volume)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1–5 of the selected parent proof (idtp_caf_rescaled_integral_tendsto), carried out for one fixed r > 0. Those steps are the setup, localisation, measurability/bounds/integrability, pointwise three-term estimate and integrated estimate.
Here R and M are hypotheses, and L is any continuous linear map satisfying (iii). In the parent:
- L = DF(b) = fderiv ℝ F b;
- R > 0 comes from HasCompactSupport.exists_pos_le_norm;
- M comes from Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support.
The statement is byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG theorem of the same name, and the argument is the same.

Notation:
- λ := Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^n;
- Φ_r(c) := r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b)) and D := B̄_{R/m}(0);
- X(c) := B.indicator J (b + rc)·f(Φ_r(c)) = 1_B(b + rc)·J(b + rc)·f(Φ_r(c)), and Y(c) := J(b)·f(Lc);
- g₁(c) := 1_{ℝ^n∖B}(b + rc) = Bᶜ.indicator (fun _ => 1) (b + rc);
- g₂(c) := |J(b + rc) − J(b)| and g₃(c) := |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Lc)|;
- G := KM·g₁ + M·g₂ + J(b)·g₃.

1. (Constants.)
- Taking w = 0 in |f(w)| ≤ M gives M ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0.
- Taking a = b in 0 ≤ J(a) ≤ K gives 0 ≤ J(b) ≤ K, so K ≥ 0.
- D is a closed ball of the proper space ℝ^n. So D is Borel and λ(D) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top).

2. (Localisation.) Let c ∉ D, i.e. |c| > R/m. Since m > 0, R < m|c|.
(a) X(c) = 0.
- If b + rc ∉ B, the factor B.indicator J (b + rc) is 0.
- If b + rc ∈ B, apply (i) with a := b + rc: m|rc| = m|(b + rc) − b| ≤ |F(b + rc) − F(b)|.
- Since r > 0, |rc| = r|c|. So |Φ_r(c)| = r^{-1}|F(b + rc) − F(b)| ≥ r^{-1}·m·r|c| = m|c| > R.
- Thus R ≤ |Φ_r(c)|, and f(Φ_r(c)) = 0 by the support hypothesis. So X(c) = 0.
(b) Y(c) = 0. By (iii), |Lc| ≥ m|c| > R, so f(Lc) = 0 and Y(c) = J(b)·0 = 0.
(c) Consequences:
- ∫_{ℝ^n} X dλ = ∫_D X dλ and ∫_{ℝ^n} Y dλ = ∫_D Y dλ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero, which needs no integrability).
- J(b)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Lc) dλ(c) = ∫_{ℝ^n} J(b)·f(Lc) dλ(c) = ∫_{ℝ^n} Y dλ (integral_const_mul, valid for every function).

3. (Measurability and bounds.)
(a) c ↦ b + rc is continuous. B.indicator J is Borel because J and B are Borel (Measurable.indicator), and Bᶜ is Borel. Hence c ↦ B.indicator J (b + rc), g₁ and g₂ are Borel.
(b) c ↦ Φ_r(c) is continuous because F is, so c ↦ f(Φ_r(c)) is continuous. c ↦ f(Lc) is continuous because L and f are. Hence:
- X, a product of a Borel and a continuous function, is Borel; so are Y and g₃;
- each of X, Y, g₁, g₂, g₃ is a.e.-strongly measurable for λ restricted to D.
(c) Bounds, for every c:
- |B.indicator J (b + rc)| ≤ K, since the value is either J(b + rc) ∈ [0, K] or 0 ≤ K. So |X(c)| ≤ KM.
- |Y(c)| = J(b)|f(Lc)| ≤ KM.
- 0 ≤ g₁(c) ≤ 1.
- 0 ≤ g₂(c) ≤ K, because J(b + rc) and J(b) both lie in [0, K].
- 0 ≤ g₃(c) ≤ |f(Φ_r(c))| + |f(Lc)| ≤ 2M.

4. (Integrability.) A function that is a.e.-strongly measurable and bounded on a set of finite measure is integrable on that set (Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded). By steps 1 and 3, X, Y, g₁, g₂ and g₃ are integrable on D. Hence so are KM·g₁, M·g₂, J(b)·g₃ and their sum G.

5. (Pointwise estimate.) Fix c ∈ ℝ^n and put u := f(Φ_r(c)) and v := f(Lc), so |u| ≤ M and |v| ≤ M.
(a) Case b + rc ∈ B. Then g₁(c) = 0 and X(c) = J(b + rc)u, so
X(c) − Y(c) = J(b + rc)u − J(b)v = (J(b + rc) − J(b))u + J(b)(u − v).
Hence |X(c) − Y(c)| ≤ |J(b + rc) − J(b)|·|u| + J(b)·|u − v| ≤ M·g₂(c) + J(b)·g₃(c) = G(c), using |u| ≤ M, g₂(c) ≥ 0 and J(b) ≥ 0.
(b) Case b + rc ∉ B. Then g₁(c) = 1 and X(c) = 0, so
|X(c) − Y(c)| = |Y(c)| = J(b)|v| ≤ J(b)M ≤ KM = KM·g₁(c) ≤ G(c).
This uses 0 ≤ J(b) ≤ K, |v| ≤ M, M ≥ 0, M·g₂(c) ≥ 0 and J(b)·g₃(c) ≥ 0.
So |X(c) − Y(c)| ≤ G(c) for every c ∈ ℝ^n.

6. (Integrated estimate.)
(a) By step 2(c) and step 4 (integral_sub):
∫_{ℝ^n} X dλ − J(b)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Lc) dλ(c) = ∫_D X dλ − ∫_D Y dλ = ∫_D (X − Y) dλ.
(b) Step 5 holds at every point, in particular λ-a.e. on D, and G is integrable on D. So |∫_D (X − Y) dλ| ≤ ∫_D G dλ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le).
(c) By step 4 and linearity (integral_add twice, integral_const_mul three times):
∫_D G dλ = KM·∫_D g₁ dλ + M·∫_D g₂ dλ + J(b)·∫_D g₃ dλ.
(d) Combining (a)–(c):
|∫_{ℝ^n} X dλ − J(b)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Lc) dλ(c)| ≤ KM·∫_D 1_{ℝ^n∖B}(b + rc) dλ(c) + M·∫_D |J(b + rc) − J(b)| dλ(c) + J(b)·∫_D |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Lc)| dλ(c).
This is the claim.
proof_key_steps: Constants: M ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0, 0 ≤ J(b) ≤ K, and λ(D) < ∞ for D = B̄_{R/m}(0).
Localisation: by (i), (iii) and f = 0 on {|w| ≥ R}, X and Y vanish off D. So ∫X = ∫_D X, and J(b)∫ f∘L = ∫Y = ∫_D Y.
X, Y, g₁, g₂, g₃ are bounded Borel functions, hence integrable on D (λ(D) < ∞).
Pointwise, |X − Y| ≤ KM·g₁ + M·g₂ + J(b)·g₃, by cases on b + rc ∈ B.
Integrate over D: |∫X − J(b)∫ f∘L| = |∫_D (X − Y)| ≤ ∫_D G = KM∫_D g₁ + M∫_D g₂ + J(b)∫_D g₃.

subproblems.title: Averages of the complement indicator vanish at a density-one point
subproblems.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, B ⊆ ℝ^n Borel and b ∈ ℝ^n. Suppose λ(B ∩ B̄_ρ(b))/λ(B̄_ρ(b)) → 1 as ρ → 0⁺, with the quotient taken in [0, ∞]. Then ⨍_{B̄_s(b)} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ → 0 as s → 0⁺. Here λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n, and the averages are Bochner set averages of the real-valued indicator function of the complement of B.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (B : Set (Euclid n)) (b : Euclid n), MeasurableSet B → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ => volume (B ∩ closedBall b ρ) / volume (closedBall b ρ)) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 1) → Tendsto (fun s : ℝ => ⨍ a in closedBall b s, Bᶜ.indicator (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) a ∂volume) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6(a)–(b) of the selected parent proof (idtp_caf_rescaled_integral_tendsto). This is the part of 'T₁(r) → 0' that turns the density-point hypothesis (iv) into vanishing ball averages of the complement indicator. The rescaling in step 6(c) is done in the parent by its sibling dependency pit_integral_closedBall_rescale_tendsto. The statement is byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG theorem of the same name, and the argument is the same.

Notation:
- λ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n, and λ_ℝ(E) := λ(E).toReal;
- for s > 0, C_s := B̄_s(b) and q(s) := λ(B ∩ C_s)/λ(C_s) ∈ [0, ∞];
- 1_{ℝ^n∖B} := Bᶜ.indicator (fun _ => 1).

1. Fix s > 0.
- C_s contains the nonempty open ball B_s(b), and Lebesgue measure charges nonempty open sets. So λ(C_s) > 0 (measure_closedBall_pos).
- C_s is a closed ball in the proper space ℝ^n, so λ(C_s) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top).
- Hence 0 < λ_ℝ(C_s); in particular λ_ℝ(C_s) ≠ 0.
2. ℝ^n∖B is Borel because B is. So ∫_{C_s} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ = ∫_{C_s ∩ (ℝ^n∖B)} 1 dλ = λ_ℝ(C_s ∖ B) (setIntegral_indicator, then setIntegral_const).
3. B is Borel and λ(C_s) ≠ ∞, so λ_ℝ(C_s ∩ B) + λ_ℝ(C_s ∖ B) = λ_ℝ(C_s) (measureReal_inter_add_sdiff). Since C_s ∩ B = B ∩ C_s, step 2 gives
∫_{C_s} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ = λ_ℝ(C_s) − λ_ℝ(B ∩ C_s).
4. By the definition of the set average (setAverage_eq),
⨍_{C_s} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ = λ_ℝ(C_s)^{-1}·∫_{C_s} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ = λ_ℝ(C_s)^{-1}(λ_ℝ(C_s) − λ_ℝ(B ∩ C_s)) = 1 − λ_ℝ(B ∩ C_s)/λ_ℝ(C_s).
The step λ_ℝ(C_s)^{-1}·λ_ℝ(C_s) = 1 uses λ_ℝ(C_s) ≠ 0 from step 1.
5. In [0, ∞], (x/y).toReal = x.toReal/y.toReal (ENNReal.toReal_div). So q(s).toReal = λ_ℝ(B ∩ C_s)/λ_ℝ(C_s). Therefore ⨍_{B̄_s(b)} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ = 1 − q(s).toReal for every s > 0.
6. By hypothesis q(s) → 1 as s → 0⁺. Since 1 ≠ ∞, toReal is continuous at 1 (ENNReal.tendsto_toReal), so q(s).toReal → 1.toReal = 1. Hence 1 − q(s).toReal → 1 − 1 = 0 as s → 0⁺.
7. The set (0, ∞) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (self_mem_nhdsWithin). On it, s ↦ ⨍_{B̄_s(b)} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ and s ↦ 1 − q(s).toReal agree by step 5. Functions that agree eventually have the same limits (Tendsto.congr'). So ⨍_{B̄_s(b)} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ → 0 as s → 0⁺, which is the claim.
No case split on n is needed. For n = 0, ℝ^0 is a single point of Lebesgue measure 1, and every B̄_s(b) with s > 0 is that point. Steps 1–7 apply verbatim.
proof_key_steps: ∫_{B̄_s(b)} 1_{ℝ^n∖B} dλ = λ_ℝ(B̄_s(b)) − λ_ℝ(B ∩ B̄_s(b)) by additivity, since B is Borel.
Hence for s > 0 the average equals 1 − q(s).toReal, where q(s) = λ(B ∩ B̄_s(b))/λ(B̄_s(b)).
toReal is continuous at 1, so 1 − q(s).toReal → 0. Transfer the limit along the identity on (0, ∞) ∈ 𝓝[>] 0.

subproblems.title: Integrated convergence of blown-up difference quotients on a ball
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, F : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, L : ℝ^n → ℝ^P a continuous linear map, b ∈ ℝ^n, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous with compact support, and R ∈ ℝ. Suppose F has Fréchet derivative L at b. Then ∫_{B̄_R(0)} |f(r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b))) − f(Lc)| dλ(c) → 0 as r → 0⁺. Here λ is Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n, B̄_R(0) = {c : |c| ≤ R}, the integral is a Bochner integral (equal to 0 by convention when the integrand is not integrable on B̄_R(0)), and no measurability of F is assumed.

Source: step 8 of the selected parent proof (idtp_caf_rescaled_integral_tendsto), 'T₃(r) → 0 from differentiability (ii)'. Here L is an arbitrary Fréchet derivative of F at b and R is an arbitrary real radius. In the parent, L = DF(b) = fderiv ℝ F b, with HasFDerivAt obtained from (ii) by DifferentiableAt.hasFDerivAt, and the radius is R_f/m > 0. Unlike the parent, S := |R| + 1 rather than R/m + 1, so that negative radii are covered. The statement is byte-identical to the comparator-accepted DAG theorem of the same name, and the argument is the same.

Notation:
- λ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n and D := B̄_R(0);
- Φ_r(c) := r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b)) and T(r) := ∫_D |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Lc)| dλ(c);
- V := λ(D).toReal and S := |R| + 1.

1. (Preliminaries.)
- D is a closed ball of the proper space ℝ^n, so λ(D) < ∞ (measure_closedBall_lt_top) and V ≥ 0.
- S > 0, and every c ∈ D satisfies |c| ≤ R ≤ |R| < S. If R < 0, then D is empty and this is vacuous.
- For every r, T(r) ≥ 0 because it is the integral of a nonnegative function (integral_nonneg).
2. Let ε > 0 and put ε₁ := ε/(V + 1) > 0.
3. (Uniform continuity.) f is continuous with compact support, hence uniformly continuous (HasCompactSupport.uniformContinuous_of_continuous). So there is η > 0 with |f(w) − f(w')| < ε₁ whenever |w − w'| < η (Metric.uniformContinuous_iff).
4. (Differentiability.) Put θ := η/(2S) > 0.
- F has Fréchet derivative L at b, so F(b + k) − F(b) − Lk = o(|k|) as k → 0 (hasFDerivAt_iff_isLittleO_nhds_zero).
- Hence |F(b + k) − F(b) − Lk| ≤ θ|k| for all k in a neighbourhood of 0.
- So there is δ₀ > 0 with |F(b + k) − F(b) − Lk| ≤ θ|k| whenever |k| < δ₀ (Metric.eventually_nhds_iff).
5. (Pointwise bound.) Put δ := δ₀/S > 0. Let 0 < r < δ and c ∈ D.
(a) |rc| = r|c| < rS < δS = δ₀, using |c| < S, r > 0 and S > 0. Hence |F(b + rc) − F(b) − L(rc)| ≤ θ|rc| = θr|c|.
(b) L is linear, so L(rc) = rLc. As r ≠ 0, Lc = r^{-1}L(rc), and Φ_r(c) − Lc = r^{-1}(F(b + rc) − F(b) − L(rc)).
(c) Hence |Φ_r(c) − Lc| = r^{-1}|F(b + rc) − F(b) − L(rc)| ≤ θ|c| ≤ θS = η/2 < η. Step 3 then gives |f(Φ_r(c)) − f(Lc)| < ε₁.
6. (Integral bound.) Let 0 < r < δ.
- By step 5, the integrand of T(r) has norm at most ε₁ at every point of D, and λ(D) < ∞.
- So |T(r)| ≤ ε₁·V (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const). This lemma needs no measurability of the integrand. If the integrand is not integrable on D, then T(r) = 0 by the Bochner convention and the bound is immediate anyway.
- With step 1, 0 ≤ T(r) ≤ ε₁V = εV/(V + 1) < ε.
7. (Conclusion.) For every ε > 0 there is δ > 0 such that |T(r) − 0| < ε whenever r ∈ (0, ∞) and |r − 0| < δ. This is exactly T(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺ (Metric.tendsto_nhdsWithin_nhds for the filter 𝓝[>] 0 = 𝓝[(0, ∞)] 0).
proof_key_steps: Set D = B̄_R(0), V = λ_ℝ(D) with λ(D) < ∞, and S = |R| + 1, so |c| < S on D; note T(r) ≥ 0.
Given ε > 0, uniform continuity of the compactly supported continuous f gives η for ε₁ = ε/(V + 1).
Differentiability at b gives δ₀ > 0 with |F(b + k) − F(b) − Lk| ≤ (η/(2S))|k| whenever |k| < δ₀.
For 0 < r < δ₀/S and c ∈ D, |Φ_r(c) − Lc| ≤ η/2 < η, so the integrand is < ε₁.
Hence 0 ≤ T(r) ≤ ε₁V < ε for 0 < r < δ₀/S, i.e. T(r) → 0 as r → 0⁺.
